items.title: A Hausdorff-dimension lower bound from subpower two-point weights on a random curve
items.source_title: Multifractal analysis of the reverse flow for the Schramm–Loewner evolution
items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs diffuse neighborhood measures from random weighted discrete samples at a vanishing radius chosen from d and xi. The proof handles diagonal self-energy and distinct active pairs separately, using subpower pair-moment loss and spatial separation to obtain a summable energy exponent for every alpha<d. These construction and energy estimates precede the already H1 Frostman/second-moment step in Lemma 10.2.
items.selected_claim: Only original Lemma 10.3 with 1<d≤m, 0<xi<1 and the exact (40)–(42) hypotheses, concluding positive probability of Hausdorff dimension at least d for the whole random curve. The separate generalization in Corollary 10.4 and the SLE verification of the abstract hypotheses are outside this selection.

source_caveats: The line before (44) on p23 prints (40) and (41). The same author already explicitly identifies the spatial separation (42) in the p22 Remark and prints it as a hypothesis, together with the moment bound (41). The original (44) and the ensuing energy comparison are retained, with the printed reference discrepancy disclosed.
The p23 diagonal upper bound uses a positive-power subpower majorant; p21 explicitly allows subpower majorants to vary by line. The radius and original displayed inequalities are retained unchanged.
The result is the abstract weighted-curve lemma. It does not require Proposition 7.2, Proposition 7.3 or Theorem 9.1, and does not establish the separate SLE conditions used later.
